_purpose: Chapter 4 builds one document up under three names. `step1.smy` is printed in full and
is committed beside this file; `step2.smy` is step1 plus a claim, and `step3.smy` is
step2 plus a definition with the claim rewritten. Neither of the later two is ever
printed as a file — the page prints the stanza that was added — so neither can be a
committed fixture without breaking the rule that a fixture is the bytes the chapter
prints. They are derived instead, which is a stronger claim: the file a command runs
against is one the book's own instructions produced.
Anchored by prose, never by content. The edit body is the fenced block following the
anchor, read out of the chapter at run time, so there is nothing here to go stale.
